title: Canonical internal-module diagonal tensor comparison
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], pulled back to the small pro-etale site of each scheme [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Write $D(X)$ for its ordinary unbounded internal-module derived category, with $Lh^*,Rh_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and tensor and unit [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For a scheme $Y$ put $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], $W=P\times_Y P$, $q:P\to Y$, $p_1,p_2:W\to P$ and $\Delta:P\to W$; use the exact supported coefficient source of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-category]. Define the canonical diagonal tensor morphism
$$d_M:p_1^*M\otimes R\Delta_*\Lambda_P\longrightarrow R\Delta_*M$$
by the existing canonical left-factor projection map of [def-sfb-proetale-projection-exchange-maps], defined from the normalized mate of [def-sfb-proetale-rational-localizing-projection-helpers] and the canonical Koszul symmetries, for $\Delta$ with arguments $p_1^*M,\Lambda_P$, and then $R\Delta_*$ of the tensor of canonical $\Delta^*p_1^*M\simeq M$ and the coefficient-unit identification, followed by the right unitor. Use its inverse for the diagonal tensor isomorphism. The section comparisons use the published derived pullback composition and identity comparisons. Use the canonical section and coefficient-unit identifications of [def-sfb-projective-diagonal-pullback] and the fixed left projection interface of [def-sfb-projective-diagonal-composition]. The unchanged composite is implemented by specializing [def-sfb-section-tensor-comparison] to $g=\Delta$, $p=p_1$, $s$ the canonical pullback section comparison, $U=\Lambda_P$ and $e$ the published single/unit comparison.

proof.text: The projective diagonal has invertible ideal. On an affine neighbourhood where its ideal is generated by r, the intersection with its open complement is the principal open D(r), hence affine. Thus the complement immersion is affine and quasi-compact over every base scheme, including the empty one.

Apply condensedSupportDerivedLocalization to the diagonal and this complement. Its closed counit is invertible. Transport the resulting composite-to-identity isomorphism using supportPullbackIsoUpperStar, leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory and rightDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory. The actual published derived closed pushforward is therefore fully faithful, so its actual adjunction counit is invertible.

For arbitrary unbounded N on the closed scheme and K on the ambient scheme, openClosedSupportProjectionFormula identifies the tensor Ri_*N tensor K with an object in the essential image of Ri_*, after transporting the exact termwise direct image to Ri_*. The essential-image criterion for a fully faithful right adjoint makes the published derived adjunction unit invertible on this tensor.

Expand the actual rightAdjointProjectionMap by its homEquiv_unit formula. Its factors are the supported unit just proved invertible, the normalized invertible derived tensor comparison, and tensor of the invertible closed counit with the identity. Hence moduleObjectProjectionMate is invertible. Both Koszul braidings are isomorphisms, so traceProjection and its uniquely normalized shared-interface realization projectionMap are invertible as well.

In sectionTensorMap the map following the projection is the direct image of tensor of the section and unit isomorphisms followed by the right unitor. This is invertible. Specialize to the existing diagonal, first projection, pullSectionIso and singleUnitIso to obtain diagonalTensorMap_isIso, without any boundedness or constructibility hypothesis.

The existing naturality argument composes the projection-mate, braiding, section and unitor naturality squares and cancels the forward diagonal tensor isomorphisms to establish naturality of their inverses.

proof_origin.place: First proof step: restriction to the diagonal and its open complement; implemented using the existing unbounded support projection and derived localization declarations. The affine-complement argument uses the Cartier diagonal already supplied by the library.
